title: Timeout heuristics synthesis and debug-view spec
content:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis of heuristics, UX wireframe writeups, and grooming notes for an integrated "request timeout" debugging surface in the Console. Focus is on production-first workflows: quickly triage timeouts (including full-request timeouts, streaming stalls, and model-run timeouts), propose root-cause hypotheses, enable safe replays, and suggest immediate mitigations (model fallback, routing change, retries).

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce mean time to triage (MTTT) for timeouts from current ~28 min to <10 min for level-2 incidents.
- Surface high-fidelity hypotheses (network vs model vs infra) with >70% accuracy on historical test set.
- Provide one-click actions to create incident notes, kick a controlled replay, or pin a fallback model.
- UX loads in <300ms for a 1k-request sampling window.

Primary personas:
- Platform SRE oncall: needs quick root-cause signal and rollback/fallback actions.
- ML engineer: wants model-level debug (token-level stalls, kv-cache anomalies, model variant differences).
- Product engineer: cares about business impact (user-facing error rate, affected routes).

Top-level surface components (wireframe descriptions):
1) Request Summary strip (horizontal header):
   - Left: request fingerprint, route name, timestamp, duration, status (timeout/5xx/model-error).
   - Middle: small stack of synthetic badges: affected model variant, region, GPU type, dedicated/pool id.
   - Right: quick actions: Replay (isolated), Pin fallback model, Create incident note, Raw export (JSON).
   - Wireframe note: badges are color-coded; timeout badge shows elapsed vs configured SLO.

2) Failure Correlator timeline (center):
   - Time-series band showing request rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate, and infra metrics (GPU utilization, host CPU, network errors).
   - Annotations auto-generated for spikes in queue depth or batch size changes.
   - Hover: show sample request thumbnails anchored to timestamp.

3) Waterfall + Token-lifecycle inspector (left column):
   - Waterfall view shows stages: ingress (client->edge), routing, queue, model-inference, outbound. Each stage annotated with mean/median/95th latency and error signals.
   - Token-lifecycle inspector shows the model-side timeline: first token emitted, KV cache warmed, last token time, streaming stalls (gaps > configured token-gap-ms).
   - Wireframe idea: use small glyphs to show where token generation stalled; click to expand token-level timeline with token-level latencies and logits heatmap (approx).

4) Request fingerprint cluster and sample set (right column):
   - Fingerprinting groups similar requests (same prompt prefix, same route headers, similar length) and shows cluster-level aggregate: timeout rate, mean duration, top 3 differing metadata fields.
   - UI affordance to narrow to a single fingerprint and open a sample gallery of raw requests and model outputs.

5) Hypothesis panel (bottom):
   - Auto-generated ranked hypotheses (e.g., "prefix-cache miss spike -> queue growth", "model N evicted -> quantization mismatch causing slow kernels", "upstream NGINX 502s causing aborted streams") with confidence score and evidence links to timeline segments and traces.
   - Each hypothesis has suggested next steps: Run isolated replay, toggle model variant, escalate to infra team, add temporary rate-limit rule to client.

6) Experimental: Delta-run comparator modal:
   - Allow side-by-side replay of two variants (live or cached) and show token-by-token time comparison, partial outputs, and per-step kernel timing (if available).
   - Useful for model regression debugging and quick validation of proposed fallback.

Interactions and keyboard shortcuts (proposed):
- / to focus quick-filter bar.
- R to start an isolated replay of selected sample (confirmation modal required).
- H to toggle hypothesis panel collapse.
- Shift+S to pin a sample to session playback.

Filtering and query language examples (console quick filters):
- timeout:true AND duration>2500ms AND region:us-west2
- status:5xx AND model:rwkv-14b-quant
- prefix_hash:0x12ab AND sample_count>5

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI surfaces request summary, timeline, waterfall, cluster list, and hypothesis panel for a sampled time window (configurable).
- Replay button triggers a backend job that replays request against a non-production pinned environment with same model version and logs results to ephemeral trace.
- Hypothesis generator returns top-3 hypotheses for >80% of sampled incidents in test corpus.
- Role-based access: replay and pin-fallback require dev/test permission; export requires audit logging.

Backlog grooming notes (ranked):
1) JIRA-INF-4321 (high) - Server-side: replay sandbox API + safe circuit breakers (2w).
2) JIRA-UI-7810 (high) - Console: timeline + waterfall base components, lazy-load metrics (1.5w).
3) JIRA-MODEL-298 (med) - Token-level timing protobuf contract between runtime and tracing (3w, infra dependency).
4) JIRA-OBS-512 (med) - Add prefix_hash field and cluster id to trace envelopes (1w).
5) JIRA-UX-944 (low) - Delta-run comparator initial UX (spikes after MVP).

Design tradeoffs and notes:
- We intentionally avoid trying to be a full flamegraph of kernel internals in MVP; instead surface coarse-grained kernel hints and hand-off to infra for deep dives.
- Sampling window should be configurable per-route; default to last 1h with up to 1k sampled requests to balance runtime cost.
- Replay sandbox must never talk to production downstreams (user databases); strip or mock out side-effects.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Raw request export must scrub PII by default; include toggle for redaction preview.
- Replays must execute under a transient service account and be recorded in audit logs.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- What should be the exact fingerprinting algorithm? (current thought: 64-bit murmur3 on sanitized prefix + route + client-type).
- How to represent streaming stalls in a way that is both compact and actionable? Proposed: show token-gap glyphs with configurable threshold.
- Hypothesis confidence: what training data and features to use? We'll iterate with a rule-based first pass (queue-depth + batch-size + evicted-models) then augment with a tiny ML model.

Handoff checklist for engineering sprint:
- [ ] API contract for sample query: fields, pagination, fingerprint id.
- [ ] Backend job for replay sandbox + result schema.
- [ ] Trace/metrics mapping: timeline buckets and tagging.
- [ ] UI components: header strip, timeline panel, waterfall component, cluster list card, hypothesis panel.
- [ ] E2E test harness: canned incidents to validate hypothesis output.

Low-fi mockup (ASCII description):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| header strip: [route: /chat/create] [timeout: 3.5s] [model: redwood-alpha-13b] [region: us-east1] [Replay] [Pin fallback] |
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| timeline (rate / timeout-rate / gpu-util)                                                  | hypothesis panel (collapsed by default)
| ────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────── |
| waterfall (ingress | queue | model | emit)       | cluster list: 5 fingerprints (click to open) |
|  [ingress: 15ms] [queue: 1200ms] [kernel: 2100ms] [emit: 90ms] | samples: 8 | timeout rate: 62%            |
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Next steps (this doc):
- Review with SRE and applied-ml next Tuesday; collect kernel-level fields that infra can provide.
- Land sampling API and prefix_hash field (obs team priority).
- Prototype simple rule-based hypothesis generator against historical incident dump (owner: Priya).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally UX-forward and contains rough engineering estimates. Please comment inline on what's infeasible or missing telemetry.
- If you have historical incident IDs that are good test cases, add to linked_artifacts or drop in slack thread.
